attempts.label: DANDI:000020

inputs.what: The paper's join of the NWB files to the Allen Patch-seq metadata (t-type, subclass, Cre line, regime membership), results/m0/m0_molecular_join.csv, which the claims file names as the paper's join of the NeMO metadata.
The retained feature lists of the three regimes, results/phenotype/phenotype_summary.json, which the claims file names; the paper's rule applied to this attempt's features gives the same lists.

attempts.entry_title: Shared type-level organization of Patch-seq phenotypes across response regimes (Yang 2026)
attempts.summary: The paper's phenotype findings hold up in this data: cell-level distances are only partly conserved across long-pulse, ramp and brief-pulse responses, local neighborhoods hardly at all, t-type explains more phenotypic variance than Cre line, and type-level distance maps are shared across the three regimes. The transcriptomic findings of Figure 4 could not be tested, because the server holding the public gene count matrix did not answer during the run. The alignment of t-type with phenotype exceeds shuffled labels as reported, but its printed sizes were not matched, and the paper's code run on its own published scores does not give them either. Most counts, such as the 57 shared t-types, equal the paper's exactly.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Yang (2026) on dandiset 000020, the Allen Institute Patch-seq recordings of mouse visual cortex in 4,435 files, most of them GABAergic interneurons. IPFX cell-level features are extracted from every file for the long-square, ramp and short-square regimes, each regime gets its own PCA phenotype space, and the cell-level and type-level comparisons of the paper are repeated with the paper's t-type labels. The transcriptomic analyses need the NeMO count matrix, which could not be fetched.

outcomes.statement: The NWB files of the dandiset are the cells of the paper's metadata join (results/m0/m0_molecular_join.csv of the paper's code at commit 61a5a41); matched by file stem, they have the same session, subject and genotype, and the same membership of the three regimes.
outcomes.source: Methods, Dataset and animals, last sentence; README of the paper's code, Data
outcomes.quote: n = 4,430 cells with a join row; n = 4,266 with a non-empty t-type
outcomes.notes: All 4,430 join rows match a file by stem (100%), and all 4,430 matched files agree with their row on session id, subject id and full genotype. Five files have no row, the four of subject 636828314 that IPFX cannot open and sub-650125704_ses-653191386. The regime membership computed here equals the join's in_long_pulse, in_ramp and in_brief_pulse for every cell (4,344, 4,139 and 4,422 in both, 0 on one side only). The join also gives two files with identical recordings different Cre lines and t-types (finding 1).

outcomes.statement: Of the cells, 4,430 have a row in the joined metadata table and 4,266 a non-empty t-type; the cells with a t-type number 4,183 in long-pulse, 3,988 in ramp and 4,266 in brief-pulse.

outcomes.statement: Built independently per regime, the phenotype spaces hold 4,344 long-pulse cells with 42 features and k80 = 11 components, 4,139 ramp cells with 20 features and k80 = 3, and 4,422 brief-pulse cells with 21 features and k80 = 5; the same-cell overlaps are 4,054 (long-pulse and ramp), 4,336 (long-pulse and brief-pulse), 4,134 (ramp and brief-pulse) and 4,049 (all three).
outcomes.source: Methods, Protocol-resolved cellular phenotype, paragraph 1; Table 1; Results, Cellular phenotypes are partially conserved, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: Resulting dataset sizes are summarized in Table 1 (long-pulse: 4,344 cells, 42 features, k 80 = 11; ramp: 4,139 cells, 20 features, k 80 = 3; brief-pulse: 4,422 cells, 21 features, k 80 = 5) ... Same-cell overlaps for cross-regime comparisons were as follows: long-pulse ∩ ramp, n = 4,054; long-pulse ∩ brief-pulse, n = 4,336; ramp ∩ brief-pulse, n = 4,134; and triple overlap, n = 4,049
outcomes.notes: The paper's rule (at most 30% missing, nonzero variance) on the features extracted here keeps exactly the paper's lists of 42, 20 and 21 features under both readings of the denominator (2a and 2b). Cells 4,344, 4,139 and 4,422; k80 11, 3 and 5 (cumulative variance 0.822, 0.883, 0.824); overlaps 4,054, 4,336, 4,134 and 4,049. Every value equals the paper's, and the cells are the ones the paper's join lists for each regime. Of 4,431 files opened, IPFX's long-square extraction failed in 87, the short-square in 9 and the ramp in 2.
deviations: Features from IPFX 2.1.2 (the current release) through its per-regime functions extract_cell_long_square_features, extract_cell_short_square_features and extract_cell_ramp_features, with the code's epoch repair and sweep filter; the paper's IPFX driver script and IPFX version are not in its code (claims file, table1-phenotype-spaces, reading 1a).

extract_ok is not defined in the paper or its code. Assumed here to be 1 when the file opened as an IPFX data set and the three regime extractions ran, each regime allowed to fail on its own, as IPFX's own cell state counts a cell failed only when every part failed. The cell sets this gives equal the paper's own regime membership (join-link), so the claims built on these spaces do not depend on the choice.

Sweeps are read from the HDF5 file with h5py in place of pynwb, for speed (patchseq._fast_reader); the notebook shows that the features, split halves and clock values equal those of IPFX's own reader on eight files across the dandiset.

Within long-pulse mean 15-NN Jaccard 0.1090, chance 0.002581 (0.002540 to 0.002582 over five shuffle seeds), adjusted 0.1064; same-pool cross-regime values 0.02537, 0.02411 and 0.02011 on pools of 3,276, 3,509 and 3,351 cells. Every value is within tolerance and the within-regime mean exceeds the three cross-regime values. The seed decides the pool. Under the seeds 1000, 2000, 3000 and 4000 the pool has 3,741, 4,100, 3,582 and 3,853 cells (random splits 501, 860, 342, 613; within 0.1095, 0.1076, 0.1082, 0.1107), and 4,100 cells and random counts of 501, 860 and 613 are out of tolerance; under the claim's seed (protocol) 3,256 cells, random 16, within 0.1071, the ramp and brief-pulse value 0.02219 just outside its tolerance and the long-pulse and ramp pool 2,946, the partial result of the first version. The within-regime mean exceeds every same-pool value under all six seeds. 806 cells failed for too few spiking sweeps to fit an f-I slope in a half under seed 0.

The random split uses seed 0, as the criterion and the code give it, because the seed decides which cells form the pool, a selection the criterion fixes; the claim's seed (protocol) and the seeds 1000 to 4000 are shown as variants, and the chance shuffles use the claim's seed.

statistics.test: Spearman A_t, empirical p against 100 label shuffles
Spearman A_t, empirical p against 100 label shuffles
Spearman A_t, empirical p against 100 label shuffles

outcomes.notes: A_t 0.0337 (long-pulse, 4,183 cells), 0.0278 (ramp, 3,988), 0.0137 (brief-pulse, 4,266), each p = 0.0099 against 100 label shuffles (null means 0.0053, 0.0012, -0.0026). None is within tolerance (ramp 0.0278 against at most 0.0275). Over the five seeds A_t is 0.0214 to 0.0337, 0.0239 to 0.0337 and 0.0137 to 0.0245, p = 0.0099 under every seed, and under no seed are all three within tolerance, so the outcome is the same under all five. A_t minus its null mean is stable over the seeds, 0.0280 to 0.0284, 0.0265 to 0.0287 and 0.0162 to 0.0182. The code's own draws under its seed 0 (variant) give 0.0292, 0.0294 and 0.0177; on the paper's own published PCA scores the same draws give 0.0370, 0.0316 and 0.0106, not the printed 0.0214, 0.0250 and 0.0213, while A_t minus null mean there (0.0264, 0.0261, 0.0161) is within 0.0005 of the paper's printed A_t minus its printed null mean (0.0264, 0.0266, 0.0166). So the printed values differ from the code's draws on the paper's scores by an offset that the null mean shares. The order the sort gives the tied 0s and 1s of the mismatch is one thing that moves A_t and its null together. With a stable sort (variant) the code's draws give 0.0350, 0.0301 and 0.0109 on the paper's scores and 0.0313, 0.0308 and 0.0180 on this attempt's, changes of at most 0.0021, with A_t minus null mean changing by at most 0.0003. These shifts are much smaller than the gap to the printed values (0.016 for long-pulse), and what produces that gap is not shown. Not run in this notebook, the executed copy of the previous run (on a CPU without AVX-512; this run's has it, cell 1) printed 0.0336, 0.0276 and 0.0135 here and 0.0368, 0.0318 and 0.0105 on the paper's scores, which is consistent with the default sort ordering ties differently on the two CPUs. The cells here are not in the order of the code's score files, so the code's draws are not the same pairs. The tie-corrected Spearman (variant) is 0.0955, 0.0848 and 0.0689. The alignment exceeds shuffled labels in every regime, as the statement says; its printed size cannot be matched to the tolerance.
deviations: Random draws use the claim's seed (protocol) in place of the code's seed 0, with four more seeds for the range given in the notes.

outcomes.statement: Cells are enriched for phenotypic neighbors of their own t-type, most for long-pulse (6.59-fold), then ramp (3.44-fold) and brief-pulse (2.64-fold).

outcomes.statement: T-types occupy distinct but overlapping parts of phenotype space, and finer t-type structure remains within single Cre-driver populations; within Sst-IRES-Cre the six most frequent t-types occupy distinct positions on long-pulse PC1.
outcomes.source: Results, Transcriptomic type anchors cellular phenotype, paragraph 1; Figure 2A,B and legend; Extended Data Figure 2-1B
outcomes.quote: transcriptomic identities occupied distinct but overlapping portions of phenotype space, and finer t-type structure remained apparent within individual Cre-driver populations
outcomes.notes: Two Cre lines of the paper's join (its cre_line includes the reporter) with at least 80 cells have the Sst-IRES-Cre driver, one with Ai14 and one with Ai167; the files' genotypes count them as one driver. With Ai14 (993 cells, 32 t-types) within-Cre A_t is 0.0313 (p 0.0099) and eta squared 0.2251 against a shuffle mean of 0.0311; with Ai167 (81 cells, 22 t-types) 0.0441 (p 0.0198) and 0.4877 against 0.2616. Both hold. Descriptive; the six most frequent t-types of the Ai14 line have long-pulse PC1 medians 0.233 to 1.844, Kruskal-Wallis p = 5.9e-19. Of the 15 lines tested, 11 have within-Cre A_t with p < 0.05 in this run (one of them at p = 0.0495).

findings.statement: Two files hold the same recording. sub-673135474_ses-680563483 and sub-673135516_ses-680897463 are from different mice, and the paper's join (Allen metadata) gives them different Cre lines (Vip-IRES-Cre and Ndnf-IRES2-dgCre), t-types (Vip Lmo1 Myl1 and Lamp5 Lsp1), layers and transcriptomic samples, yet the voltage traces of all their usable long squares are identical (SHA-1) and so are all 94 of their IPFX features. At most one of the two cells' recordings is in the dandiset, and one file carries another cell's data. No other two files share a trace or a feature vector.
findings.checked: The outputs show it: in cell 9 the two files share an identical fingerprint, an identical long-square hash and identical IPFX feature vectors, and no other pair of files matches; in cell 11 the join gives them different Cre lines, t-types (Vip Lmo1 Myl1 / Lamp5 Lsp1), layers (VISp2/3 / VISp4) and transcriptomic samples (S010 / S012); the subjects differ by path (cell 7). Not printed: the "all 93 of their IPFX features" count for this pair. Critical is the right rating: one file carries another cell's recording under different metadata, and nothing in the files flags it; the effect on any statistic here is negligible, but the rating depends on the kind of error, not its effect.

findings.statement: The four files of subject 636828314 (sessions 637823738, 637824890, 637833126, 637838825) list two response series for sweep number 1 in their sweep table, so IPFX cannot open them. The paper's join has no row for them either.

The files hold no transcriptomic label or sample identifier; the t-types, subclasses and RNA sample ids of these Patch-seq cells come only from the Allen metadata, joined by session or file name. The Cre line can be read from the subject genotype, which agrees with the Allen metadata for every cell.

Every count the paper reports for the dataset is in the files; 4,435 files, 4,430 joined to the paper's metadata, and IPFX features that give the paper's 4,344, 4,139 and 4,422 cells per regime, its 42, 20 and 21 retained features and its k80. Sessions and subjects in the files equal the paths, and the voltage response of every cell's most hyperpolarizing long square begins at the stimulus onset (median change 0.01 mV in the 10 ms before onset, -15.3 mV 15 to 25 ms after), so stimulus and response share a clock.

paper_notes.statement: Question for the paper's author. The code does not hold the script that ran IPFX on all cells: which IPFX version and call made results/features/ipfx_cell_features.csv, and what sets extract_ok = 1? This attempt used IPFX 2.1.2 through its per-regime functions and took extract_ok = 1 for a file that opened and ran; the resulting cells and features equal the paper's, so the choice made no difference here, but the paper should state it. The script that wrote results/q3b/q3b_primary_null_1000.csv (Table 2 rows m and n) is also missing.

The A_t values of Table 2 (rows d to i) depend on an arbitrary order. The code ranks the binary t-type mismatch with np.argsort(np.argsort(x)), so the tied 0s and 1s are ordered as the sort leaves them, and the coefficient carries an offset, shared with its null, that moves with the pair sample and with the order of the tied ranks (a stable sort moves A_t by up to 0.0021 and A_t minus the null mean by at most 0.0003). Run with the code's own draws and seed 0 on the paper's published PCA scores, it gives A_t 0.0370, 0.0316 and 0.0106 against the printed 0.0214, 0.0250 and 0.0213, while A_t minus the null mean (0.0264, 0.0261, 0.0161) is within 0.0005 of the printed difference (0.0264, 0.0266, 0.0166); what produces the larger gap in A_t itself is not shown. The significance against shuffles holds; the printed values have less precision than their three decimals suggest, and A_t minus the null mean, or the tie-corrected Spearman, would be reproducible.

In the split-half analysis the random fallback split draws its permutation from a generator made afresh with seed 0 for each cell, so every cell with the same number of sweeps gets the same permutation, and the seed decides which cells form the pool. With seed 0 this attempt gets the paper's 3,598 cells exactly (358 random splits); with the seeds 1000 to 4000 the pool has 3,582 to 4,100 cells, and with another seed 3,256. The paper reports the pool without saying that it depends on the seed.

entries.name: chartrand-2023
entries.title: Human layer 1 interneuron electrophysiology (Chartrand et al. 2023)
entries.description: Tests the electrophysiology findings of Chartrand et al. (2023) on dandiset 000630, which holds the current clamp recordings of the paper's 210 Seattle human L1 patch-seq cells. Features are extracted with IPFX from the long square sweeps and compared with the paper's per-cell table; cell types come from the paper's cell table, linked by the LIMS identifier. A second notebook compares the human cells with the paper's mouse L1 cells from dandiset 000020. A third notebook tests four morphology claims on the paper's deposited morphology features.

entries.name: mansvelder-2026
entries.title: Resonance of human and mouse cortical interneurons (Shamugia et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Shamugia, Weiler, ... Goriounova and Mansvelder (2026) on human cortical interneuron resonance on dandiset 000630 (210 human layer 1 interneurons, Chartrand et al. 2023), with dandiset 000636 (human acute and slice-culture interneurons, Lee, Dalley et al. 2023) and the paper's mouse cells in dandiset 000020 (Gouwens et al. 2020). The notebook computes impedance profiles, resonance frequency and strength, sag ratio and input resistance, and tests how they differ between species, preparations, regions and diseases, how they relate, and how they relate to ion channel gene expression. The depth, ZD7288, Allen Brain Map and modelling findings are not tested.

entries.name: yang-2026-flexible
entries.title: Shared type-level organization of Patch-seq phenotypes across response regimes (Yang 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Yang (2026) on dandiset 000020, the Allen Institute Patch-seq recordings of mouse visual cortex in 4,435 files, most of them GABAergic interneurons. IPFX cell-level features are extracted from every file for the long-square, ramp and short-square regimes, each regime gets its own PCA phenotype space, and the cell-level and type-level comparisons of the paper are repeated with the paper's t-type labels. The transcriptomic analyses need the NeMO count matrix, which could not be fetched.
